entry.title: The retracted claim is the nearer match
entry.summary: Agent memory that keeps its history holds both the claim and the correction, and on cosine similarity the retracted claim often wins. One pair of memos from RE-call's shipped demo corpus shows the failure exactly, why a better ranker cannot fix it, and how declared supersession on PostgreSQL and pgvector does: every hit carries a verdict, the stale memo comes back marked superseded, and a question the corpus cannot answer is refused with a measured margin.
